verification_results.self_report_mismatch_reason: The 'deviations' entry for reviewer resolution (b) asserts 'no real source can carry a block-level version>1 today via this parser's own grammar' as grounds for not implementing LogOptError::UnsupportedVersion. This is materially false: version:2 (or any int) is trivially parseable as the block-level `version` field (only an *unknown block-level KEY* is unreachable, not a *version number greater than 1*). Empirically reproduced end-to-end below.

top_priority_finding_deviation_2.task_question: Is deviation 2's premise correct, and is AT-2924 testing something real, and is section 1.4a's preserve-and-warn promise vacuous?
top_priority_finding_deviation_2.determination: DEVIATION 2 IS WRONG. FAIL-grade finding, per the explicit criterion given for this investigation.
evidence: 1. Constructed /tmp scratchpad v2_block.axc: @optimization_log { version: 2, entry {...one valid v1-shaped entry...} }. `axc verify` → Pass, 0 errors, 0 warnings. `axc compile` → exit 0. This proves the parser DOES produce a real, on-disk, HIR-valid version>1 block — directly contradicting the coder's 'no real source can carry a block-level version>1' claim.

2. Ran `axc log-opt v2_block_towrite.axc --kernel v2_block --metric 99999 --unit mtflops --verdict PASS --ts ...` against that v2 block. Result: exit 0, JSON {"status":"ok"} — the writer SPLICED a v1-shaped entry into the version:2 block WITHOUT refusal and WITHOUT any warning. `grep LogOptError crates/axc-driver/src/log_opt.rs` confirms no `UnsupportedVersion` variant exists at all (only Full, Multikernel, Parse, MalformedExistingBlock, NoAnchor, Io).

3. Re-ran `axc verify` on the post-append file: Pass, 0 errors, 0 warnings — the schema-version mixing the pessimistic design reviewer's SHOULD-FIX #2 (M3.19-pessimistic-design-review.json warnings[1]) explicitly warned about ('splicing a v1 entry into a v2 block... silently mixes schema versions inside one block') is now silently present in the file with zero diagnostic trace.

4. Separately confirmed the ONE part of the coder's claim that IS true: an unknown BLOCK-LEVEL key (any version) is genuinely unreachable via real parsed source — v1_block_unknown_key.axc with `future_field: 7` at block scope → real PARSE error 'expected `entry` or `version`', regardless of the declared version number. This is because block_item is EBNF-closed to version_field|entry_block — confirmed by inspecting parser.rs's parse_optimization_log_block. The coder conflated 'block-level unknown KEY is unreachable' (true) with 'block-level version>1 is unreachable' (false) — a real error in the technical justification, not a semantic quibble.

5. Checked what AT-2924 actually exercises: crates/axc-hir/src/opt_log.rs lines 596-610. Both at_2924_v2_unknown_block_key_preserved_not_rejected AND at_2924_v2_unknown_entry_key_preserved_known_fields_still_validated construct RecordField values directly via a Rust-level `field()` helper — NOT through the parser. So AT-2924 is a pure HIR-unit-level test of validate_block/validate_entry's preserve-and-warn logic in isolation; it does not by itself prove the promise is reachable end-to-end.

6. HOWEVER: I independently constructed real parsed source with an UNKNOWN ENTRY-LEVEL key inside a version:2 block (v2_entry_unknown.axc, future_field:7 inside entry{}) and ran it through `axc verify`/`axc compile`. Result: HirWarning::UnknownOptimizationLogKeyForward correctly fires, the file compiles successfully (0 errors), and forward_unknown is populated. This proves the entry-level direction of section 1.4a's preserve-and-warn promise IS real and delivered end-to-end via the real parser+HIR — it is NOT vacuous for the practically relevant channel (this is also what AT-2925's byte-verbatim round-trip actually exercises).
top_priority_finding_deviation_2.conclusion: Two separable claims must not be conflated: (a) '#1.4a preserve-and-warn is vacuous' — FALSE, independently disproven; the entry-level direction works end-to-end through real source, only the block-level direction is dead code by construction of the closed EBNF (and this is honestly disclosed by the coder in known_limitations). (b) 'the writer safely handles an existing version>1 block' — FALSE and NOT disclosed accurately; the writer silently splices into it, exactly the unsafe scenario the pessimistic reviewer flagged, and the coder's justification for skipping the fix rests on a factually incorrect premise (that the scenario is unreachable, when it is directly reachable by any hand-authored or future-writer-produced v2 file).
top_priority_finding_deviation_2.severity_and_scope_note: The pessimistic design review (M3.19-pessimistic-design-review.json) filed this as a SHOULD-FIX under an overall APPROVE verdict, not a blocking MUST-FIX in the adopted r2 spec (section 8 lists only 3 official must-fixes, none of which is 'writer refuses version>1'). So strictly under the r2 contract this omission alone would be a should-fix gap, not automatically FAIL. What elevates it to FAIL here is that the coder's self-report affirmatively claims the scenario is 'structurally' impossible and uses that (incorrect) claim as the basis for skipping the fix — an unverified/false technical claim in the self-report, which is exactly the class of 'agents lie about their own work' the QA process exists to catch, plus a demonstrated real safety gap (silent schema-version mixing with zero diagnostic) that a future consumer would hit.
top_priority_finding_deviation_2.recommended_fix: Small, well-scoped: in splice_optimization_log_entry (crates/axc-driver/src/log_opt.rs), after parsing/validating the existing block, check parsed_version > SUPPORTED_OPT_LOG_VERSION and return LogOptError::UnsupportedVersion{found, supported} (source byte-unchanged, new exit code), plus one AT. Estimated ~15-25 LOC + 1 test.

summary: Build, clippy, and full test suite (1217 passed / 0 failed / 132 ignored, +67 new tests, zero regressions vs the 1150/132 baseline) are all clean, and I independently re-verified essentially every acceptance test named in the QA brief (AT-2903, AT-2907, AT-2913, AT-2915..2925, AT-2919/2920/2921) plus 4 of my own adversarial grammar fixtures, the writer's 64-entry cap and multikernel fail-closed paths, a live MCP JSON-RPC call, and confirmed the scope discipline (codegen 1 mechanical line, lexer/runtime untouched). All of that is genuinely solid. But the TOP-PRIORITY deviation-2 investigation surfaces a real problem: the coder's justification for skipping the pessimistic reviewer's SHOULD-FIX ('writer refuses to append into a version>1 block') is factually wrong — I built a real, parseable, HIR-valid version:2 block by hand and then ran the real `axc log-opt` writer against it: it silently spliced a v1-shaped entry into the v2 block with exit 0 and zero warnings, exactly the schema-version-mixing risk the reviewer flagged. The coder's self-report claims this scenario is 'structurally' unreachable via the parser, but only the narrower claim (unknown BLOCK-LEVEL key is unreachable) is true — version>1 itself is trivially reachable. Section 1.4a's preserve-and-warn promise is NOT vacuous overall (the entry-level forward-compat direction is real and independently verified end-to-end), but the writer-side safety gap is real, undisclosed accurately, and unfixed. Combined with an undisclosed ~2.8x LOC budget overrun, verdict is FAIL — recommend a small, scoped fix (add LogOptError::UnsupportedVersion to the writer, ~15-25 LOC + 1 AT) and a corrected self-report, then re-submit for QA.
